chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: Was Armstrong an Uncle Tom
summary: JCH says Armstrong and Red Allen were both Uncle Toms who took their money without saying yes sir.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Did he ever talk about his life or anything at all? Did he say anything to you?

You say that he was a pretty strong and outspoken man. One of the things that maybe you can help to correct: you know, a lot of people of the younger generation looked at Louis Armstrong as being an Uncle Tom. How would you feel about that?

How so? How can anybody be one? Just an Uncle Tom, period, he and Red Allen. He worked and he got his money, but he didn't go around and say, yes sir, and you know, things like that. He didn't do that, no.
Why would you say then that he was an Uncle Tom?
I don't know how to explain it.
But you just felt that he was?
The people were correct in saying that?
Red Allen was the same way. I told you that. He admitted it.
